prose.title: React/DOM Properties
prose.text:
At its core, the FormField component is a regular <div> element. Thus, both DOM and React properties, methods, and events are accessible. To read up on all of the possible DOM attributes and types available for div elements, check out this [MDN Web Documents page.](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/div) To learn more about DOM events and methods, you can read more on the [MDN Web Events documentation page](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Events).

Also, feel free to read about the [types of React events available](https://reactjs.org/docs/handling-events.html), or see [how DOM attributes change in React.](https://reactjs.org/docs/dom-elements.html) Working in tandem with Styled Components, you also have access to the [as property.](https://styled-components.com/docs/api#as-polymorphic-prop)

The component to insert in the FormField. Grommet will update the
            form values when this field changes. Any additional properties (such
            as initial value) you pass to FormField will be forwarded to this
            component. The component may be custom as long it supports the
            properties of name, value, onChange (event => {}), while event has
            either event.value or event.target.value.

**NOTE**: In order to use validate, a name must first be provided to the FormField.

If a function is provided, it will be called with two arguments, the value for this field and the entire value object. This permits validation to encompass multiple fields. The function should return a string message describing the validation issue, if any, or an object with 'message' and 'status' properties.
